_comment: Best model per Comet project, hand-curated. Refresh candidate metrics with
which rewrites metrics from Comet but NEVER changes 'best'. Promoting a model
is a judgement about fitness, not an argmax over a leaderboard -- dogbin_001
tops its project and is still not deployable (see its note).
A null 'best' means nothing has earned the slot yet; it is never filled with
URLs are NOT stored: they are built from url_template + workspace + the
project name + the experiment key, so this file carries no hardcoded links.
stage/short/emits/key_metric drive the pipeline view: the three projects are one chain, and a stage with best:null stops everything downstream of it.

dogdetection.role: detector - finds ground animals in street imagery (the sweep runs this)

best.why: In production: this is the engine sweeping all 32.5M images. Best mAP50-95 (0.4973) and best recall (0.8764) in the project. train-28 edges it on mAP50 by 0.0008 but loses 3.4 points of recall, and recall is what matters when a missed dog is unrecoverable and a false positive is one click in the review page.

dog-bin.role: binary gate - dog vs not_dog, runs before the leash classifier
dog-bin.why_blank: No model has earned it yet. dogbin_001 tops the project on top-1 (0.9652) but that split leaked: 70.8% of its val images shared a Mapillary sequence with train, and on the sequence-clean remainder it scores 0.9213. Worse, on real sweep false positives it rejects only 16% at t=0.5 with median P(dog)=0.9998 -- unusable as a gate. dogbin_002 was the first run on a leak-free split but was killed at epoch 329 of 500 and never converged. dogbin_003 converged and is a genuinely working gate, but its acceptance test was contaminated and at the only threshold that loses no dogs it rejects 45.4%; it is a candidate, not a promotion. dogbin_004 trains on dogbin_v4, the first dataset built with a permanent acceptance set reserved BEFORE the split (data/dogbin_acceptance_set.json, 214 image_ids) and with embedding-based near-duplicate removal. Nothing gets promoted on top-1 alone: the gate criterion is rejection rate on real sweep false positives at a threshold that preserves dog recall, which is what disqualified dogbin_001 despite the highest top-1 in the project.

candidates.dataset: dogbin_v3 (sequence-clean split + dashboard-flagged hard negatives folded in as extra negatives)
candidates.note: Converged: early-stopped at epoch 281/500, best at 181, patience 100. The first dog-bin run that is both leak-free AND finished. Far better than dogbin_001 as a gate -- on real sweep false positives it rejects 70.3% at t=0.5 with median P(dog) 0.0190, against dogbin_001's 16% at median 0.9998. NOT PROMOTED, for two reasons. (1) The first measurement was contaminated: 360 of the 1072 flagged crops in data/hard_negatives/crops are the same detections rebuild_crop_dataset.py folded into dogbin_v3 as extra negatives -- 297 in train, 63 in val. The collision is invisible by filename (dataset uses flag_<image_id>_<det>.jpg, the flag dir uses <ts>_<image_id>_<conf>.jpg) and only shows up when matching on image_id. Removing them moved rejection at t=0.5 from 0.7740 [0.747,0.799] to 0.7032 [0.669,0.736] -- disjoint intervals -- and median P(dog) from 0.0043 to 0.0190. eval_dogbin.py now excludes them automatically. (2) At the only threshold that loses no dogs (t=0.0086, val recall 1.0000) it rejects just 45.4% [0.418,0.491] of real false positives. Every headline figure is quoted at t>=0.5, which costs 5 of 326 val dogs; on a one-pass sweep a missed dog is unrecoverable. To promote: harvest a batch of flagged false positives that has never been passed to --extra-negatives, hold it out permanently, and quote rejection at a recall-preserving threshold measured against production dogs rather than 326 annotator crops.

TERMINATED, not converged. Best top-1 0.9421 at epoch 299 against a 0.7283 majority-class prior; the run died at epoch 329 of 500 when a `git stash -u` swept away the leash_models symlink and the results-CSV path stopped resolving. Patience was 100, so it was still 71 epochs from an honest early stop -- 0.9421 is where it happened to be when it was killed, not where it settled. NOT comparable to dogbin_001 (different val set) nor to dogbin_003 (v3 adds the flagged hard negatives).
Rejected as a gate. The headline number is inflated by leakage and it fails on the distribution it must actually survive.

leash-models.role: leash classifier - leashed vs unleashed, on crops the gate passes
leash-models.why_blank: Nothing here has been verified against a leak-free split, and no leash model is wired into the sweep yet (the panel still reads 'classifier not wired in yet'). The runs below are the top scorers by reported top-1, but every one predates the sequence-leak finding, so their numbers are suspect for the same reason dogbin_001's were. The 3-class variant was measured and rejected: it discarded 15.5% of real dogs at a mean confidence of 0.87, which is why the binary gate exists.

candidates.note: Highest top-1 in the project. Unverified: split not checked for sequence leakage.
REJECTED. The 3-class experiment (leashed/unleashed/not_a_dog) that the binary gate replaced.
